stem: A 27-year-old man has intensely itchy small grouped blisters and scratch marks over his elbows, knees and buttocks for 2 months. He also reports bloating and loose stools after eating bread. A perilesional skin biopsy is sent for direct immunofluorescence.
oneliner: 27M + intensely itchy grouped vesicles on elbows, knees, buttocks + bloating and loose stools after bread → which DIF pattern?
ask: Which direct immunofluorescence pattern is most likely?

options.A: Linear IgG along the basement membrane
options.B: Granular IgA deposits at the tips of the dermal papillae
options.C: Intercellular IgG in a net-like epidermal pattern
options.D: Linear IgA along the basement membrane
options.E: Granular IgG and C3 at the dermal-epidermal junction

whyNot.A: The pattern of **bullous pemphigoid**, which gives large tense bullae in the elderly, not **small grouped** vesicles in a 27-year-old
whyNot.C: The **pemphigus** pattern, with flaccid blisters and mucosal erosions, not this itchy grouped eruption
whyNot.D: **Linear IgA disease** gives a linear band and is not tied to **gluten-related bowel symptoms**
whyNot.E: The **lupus band** pattern; his itchy extensor vesicles with **gluten-triggered bowel symptoms** do not fit lupus

answer: Granular IgA at the dermal papillary tips (dermatitis herpetiformis)
why: **Dermatitis herpetiformis** is the skin manifestation of **celiac disease**. IgA against **epidermal transglutaminase** deposits as **granular IgA at the tips of the dermal papillae**, with neutrophil microabscesses and subepidermal blisters. It improves with **dapsone and a gluten-free diet**.

idea.rule: Itchy extensor vesicles + gluten symptoms = granular IgA in dermal papillae (dermatitis herpetiformis).
also: Associated antibodies: anti-tissue transglutaminase and anti-endomysial
HLA-DQ2/DQ8 associated
Bullous pemphigoid: linear IgG and C3 at the basement membrane
Pemphigus vulgaris: intercellular IgG, 'chicken-wire' pattern

stem: An 80-year-old man has several weeks of itchy tense blisters on his thighs and in the skin folds. His mouth is not involved. A biopsy shows a split beneath the epidermis, and a second biopsy of nearby normal-looking skin is sent for direct immunofluorescence.
oneliner: 80M + itchy tense blisters on thighs and flexures + mouth spared + subepidermal split → which direct immunofluorescence pattern?
ask: Which direct immunofluorescence pattern is most likely?

options.A: Intercellular, net-like IgG around the keratinocytes
options.B: Granular IgA at the tips of the dermal papillae
options.C: Granular IgG and C3 in a band at the dermoepidermal junction
options.D: Linear IgG and C3 along the basement membrane zone

whyNot.A: That net pattern marks **acantholysis** (pemphigus); his split lies **beneath the epidermis**, not within it
whyNot.B: Seen in **dermatitis herpetiformis**, with grouped itchy vesicles on elbows and buttocks; he has **large tense blisters on flexures**
whyNot.C: A **lupus band** accompanies lupus erythematosus, not a **tense bullous eruption** in an elderly man
whyNot.E: Immunofluorescence is **positive** in an autoimmune subepidermal blistering disease; only a **non-immune cause** would be negative

answer: Linear IgG and C3 along the basement membrane
why: An elderly patient with **tense, itchy bullae**, **spared mouth** and a **subepidermal split** has **bullous pemphigoid**. IgG against **hemidesmosome proteins (BP180, BP230)** fixes complement, which gives a **smooth linear line** along the basement membrane zone.

idea.rule: Pemphigoid is a line (linear along the basement membrane); pemphigus is a net (intercellular).
also: Pemphigus vulgaris: net-like IgG between keratinocytes
Dermatitis herpetiformis: granular IgA in dermal papillary tips
Linear IgA bullous disease: linear IgA at the basement membrane
Lupus: granular 'lupus band' of Ig and complement at the junction

stem: A 45-year-old woman has painful erosions in her mouth for two months, followed by thin-roofed blisters on her trunk that break easily and leave raw areas. Gentle sideways pressure on normal-looking skin makes the top layer slide off. A biopsy shows a split just above the basal cell layer, and direct immunofluorescence is performed.
oneliner: 45F + painful oral erosions then flaccid ruptured blisters + sliding skin on pressure + suprabasal split → which direct immunofluorescence pattern?
ask: Which direct immunofluorescence pattern is most likely?

options.A: Linear IgG and C3 along the basement membrane
options.C: Granular IgA at the dermal papillary tips
options.D: Linear IgA along the basement membrane
options.E: IgA in the walls of small dermal vessels

whyNot.A: That is **pemphigoid**, with a split **under** the epidermis; her split lies **just above the basal cells**, within the epidermis
whyNot.C: That marks **dermatitis herpetiformis** (celiac skin disease), with intensely itchy grouped vesicles, not **painful mouth erosions** and sliding skin
whyNot.D: That is **linear IgA bullous disease**, a **subepidermal** blister; her blister roof is **thin and intraepidermal**
whyNot.E: That fits **IgA vasculitis (Henoch-Schonlein)** with **palpable purpura**, not blisters and oral erosions

why: **Painful oral erosions, flaccid blisters, Nikolsky sign and a suprabasal split** make this **pemphigus vulgaris**. IgG against **desmoglein 3** (with desmoglein 1) disrupts desmosomes between keratinocytes, so immunofluorescence shows a **'fishnet' of IgG around each cell**.

idea.rule: Pemphigus gives a net between cells (desmosomes); pemphigoid gives a line at the basement membrane (hemidesmosomes).
also: Pemphigus foliaceus: anti-desmoglein 1, granular-layer split, no mouth involvement
Pemphigus vulgaris: anti-desmoglein 3, suprabasal split, mouth first
Paraneoplastic pemphigus occurs with lymphoma
Tombstone basal cells are the histology clue

stem: A 78-year-old woman has weeks of intense itching with red, urticarial plaques on her thighs and groin. New blisters then appear on top of these plaques. Serum contains IgG against hemidesmosomal proteins.
oneliner: 78F + itchy urticarial plaques then blisters on thighs and groin + IgG against hemidesmosome proteins → which clinical finding?
ask: Which additional clinical finding is most likely?

options.A: Thin, flaccid blisters that rupture into raw erosions
options.B: Painful erosions of the oral mucosa as the first sign
options.C: Grouped itchy vesicles on the elbows and buttocks
options.E: Large tense blisters with the mouth spared

whyNot.A: That is the **intraepidermal** picture of pemphigus; her antibodies target **hemidesmosomes**, so the split lies deeper and the roof is thick
whyNot.B: Typical of **pemphigus vulgaris** (desmoglein 3, a mucosal antigen); her IgG targets **hemidesmosomes** and she has **itchy urticarial plaques**
whyNot.C: That is **dermatitis herpetiformis**, with granular IgA; her serum has **IgG to hemidesmosomes** and lesions sit on **thighs and groin** after urticarial plaques
whyNot.D: That is **erythema multiforme**, usually after HSV or drugs; she has **blisters on urticarial plaques**, not targets

answer: Large tense blisters with an intact mouth
why: **Antibodies to hemidesmosome proteins (BP180/BP230)** cause a split **between the epidermis and dermis**, so the whole epidermis forms a **thick roof** and the blisters stay **tense**. The urticarial phase with **itch**, elderly onset and little mucosal disease complete **bullous pemphigoid**.

idea.rule: Deeper split (subepidermal) means a thick roof: tense blisters, rarely erosions, little mouth disease.
also: Pemphigus vulgaris: intraepidermal split, flaccid blisters, Nikolsky positive, mouth erosions
Epidermolysis bullosa acquisita: anti-type VII collagen, subepidermal, tense blisters
Linear IgA bullous disease: subepidermal split with tense blisters
Dermatitis herpetiformis is also subepidermal, so its small vesicles are tense

stem: A 50-year-old man has anti-desmoglein 3 IgG in his serum. A biopsy of a skin lesion shows a split just above the basal layer within the epidermis, and gentle rubbing of normal skin causes the surface to slough.
oneliner: 50M + anti-desmoglein 3 IgG + suprabasal split + sloughing on rubbing → which early finding?
ask: Which early clinical finding is most likely?

options.A: Tense blisters in the skin folds with an intact mouth
options.B: Painful mouth erosions, later flaccid blisters
options.C: Grouped itchy vesicles on the elbows
options.D: Honey-colored crusted erosions around the nose

whyNot.A: Tense roofs and a spared mouth fit **pemphigoid**; his **suprabasal split** and anti-desmoglein 3 point to the opposite picture
whyNot.C: That is **dermatitis herpetiformis**, linked to **celiac disease**, with granular IgA; his antibody is **anti-desmoglein 3**
whyNot.D: That is **impetigo**, a bacterial infection with no **desmoglein antibodies** or suprabasal split
whyNot.E: That is **erythema multiforme**; his **Nikolsky-positive** blistering with anti-desmoglein 3 is autoimmune and intraepidermal

answer: Painful oral erosions first, then flaccid blisters
why: **Desmoglein 3** is strongly expressed in the **mucosa** and deep epidermis, so antibodies against it produce **oral erosions first** and later fragile **flaccid skin blisters** at the **suprabasal** level. Pemphigus vulgaris is often present in the mouth for months before the skin.

idea.rule: Desmoglein 3 predominates in mucosa and basal layers, so anti-desmoglein 3 disease starts in the mouth.
also: Pemphigus foliaceus (anti-desmoglein 1 only) spares the mouth
Mucosal-dominant pemphigus vulgaris has anti-desmoglein 3 alone; adding anti-desmoglein 1 brings skin disease
SSSS toxin cleaves desmoglein 1, so the mouth is spared
Paraneoplastic pemphigus also targets desmoglein 3 and gives severe stomatitis

stem: A 3-year-old girl has fever, irritability and widespread tender red skin. Large floppy blisters have appeared in the armpits and groin, and the top layer peels with light rubbing. Her mouth is not affected. Two days earlier she had a crusted sore beside her nose. Fluid is drawn from an unbroken bulla for Gram stain and culture.
oneliner: 3F + fever + tender red skin + flaccid bullae, mouth spared + crusted nasal sore 2 days earlier → what does the blister fluid show?
ask: Which result is expected from the bulla fluid?

options.C: Multinucleated giant cells on a Tzanck smear

whyNot.A: That would mean **bacteria inside the blister**; here the damage comes from a **toxin made at the nose**, far from the bulla
whyNot.B: Streptococci cause **impetigo or erysipelas** at the site they infect; her blisters are **widespread in armpits and groin**, far from the **nasal sore**
whyNot.C: That points to **HSV or VZV** with grouped vesicles on an erythematous base, not a **desquamating toxin** syndrome
whyNot.E: That suggests **Pseudomonas or enteric infection** in a sick or immunocompromised child; her trigger is a **crusted nasal sore**

why: This is **staphylococcal scalded skin syndrome**: **exfoliative toxins A and B** from a distant **Staphylococcus aureus** focus (here the nose) travel in blood and **cleave desmoglein 1** in the granular layer. The bulla therefore contains **no bacteria**, the **mouth is spared**, and the roof is very thin.

idea.rule: In SSSS the toxin travels but the bug stays home, so the blister fluid is sterile.
also: Bullous impetigo is the localized form, where the blisters do contain S. aureus
Exfoliative toxin cleaves desmoglein 1 and spares desmoglein 3 in the mouth
Toxic shock syndrome: TSST-1 spreads from a local focus (tampon, wound), and blood cultures are usually negative
Diphtheria toxin damages the heart and nerves while the bacteria stay in the throat
